run.task: Queue item #2: verify or refute the claim that ProductRepository.findAllDashboard paginates in memory (HHH90003004) because it combines LEFT JOIN FETCH p.pairings with a Pageable.

criteria.statement: Given the dashboard product listing is requested with a page size smaller than the catalog, when the issued SQL is inspected, then the row limit is applied by the database and no in-memory pagination warning is logged.
criteria.notes: Refutes the claim. Hibernate 7.4.1 emits: `... from (select distinct p1_0.* from products p1_0 left join product_translations ... order by p1_0.created_at desc offset ? rows fetch first ? rows only) p1_0 left join product_pairings ...` — the limit is inside the DISTINCT derived table, before the collection join, so the fetch-join multiplication applies to one page only. HHH90003004 occurs 0 times in the whole container log. page=1 (non-zero OFFSET) carries the same limit clause, which is the case in-memory pagination would hide.

criteria.statement: Given any page, when the pages are walked, then their union is exactly the catalog with no duplicate and no skipped row.
criteria.notes: page=0/1/2 at size=3 over a 7-product catalog returned [1,2,3], [4,5,6], [7] with last=true on the final page — identical to the unpaged read of the same catalog, no duplicate and no gap. Recorded as a guard, not as discrimination: in-memory pagination would also return correct pages, which is why PP-01 asserts on the SQL instead.

criteria.statement: Given the listing is filtered (category slug, search, active), when it is paged, then the limit is still applied by the database.
criteria.notes: categorySlug=coffee (2 of 4), search=e (2 of 5) and isActive=true (2 of 7) each issued a row query still carrying `offset ? rows fetch first ? rows only`.
